correction.supersedes: Prior source note attributed H1 $8.82T and USDC 70% to Cointelegraph.
correction.corrected_scope: Cointelegraph supports June $1.79T adjusted volume and USDC 67% June share. Finst supports H1 $8.82T adjusted volume and USDC about 70% H1 share. Both cite Visa/Allium; source attributions are now separate.
correction.preservation: Prior source records remain immutable; correction is appended.

confirmed_facts.claim: Circle's October 16 blog claims USDC captured about 77% of global stablecoin transaction volume in June 2026 and settled more than $36T onchain in H1.
confirmed_facts.qualification: Issuer/company claim; methodology not fully specified in the cited blog.

confirmed_facts.claim: Cointelegraph's July 6 report says Visa/Allium adjusted stablecoin volume reached $1.79T in June 2026 and USDC accounted for about 67% of June adjusted volume.
Finst's July 6 report says Visa/Allium adjusted stablecoin volume reached $8.82T in H1 2026 and USDC accounted for about 70% of H1 adjusted volume.
Visa's official dashboard describes adjusted transaction volume that filters bots and other inorganic/programmatic activity.

inferences.claim: Circle's 77% June company-reported volume share and Visa/Allium's 67% adjusted June share should be treated as different methodologies/denominators, not a direct contradiction.
inferences.basis: Issuer blog does not specify the same adjustment methodology; Visa explicitly adjusts for inorganic activity.

inferences.claim: The H1 70% USDC share is a separate period measure and must not be attributed to the Cointelegraph June article.
inferences.basis: Direct page inspection: Finst article contains the H1 $8.82T/70% figures; Cointelegraph article contains June $1.79T/67%.

unknowns: Circle's precise transaction-volume methodology and its reconciliation to Visa/Allium adjusted volume.
The exact share of Circle's $36T H1 figure attributable to organic payment/settlement versus exchange transfers, bot activity, bridge routing and internal smart-contract operations.
